title: A Compass for the Rivergate
premise: Zephyrine Halloran, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Rivergate Syndicate, discovers a tide-revealed cave holding a compass that points not north but toward whatever its bearer most needs to survive. The Syndicate wants it; so does a fugitive cartographer named Ivo who claims it was stolen from his family. Hunted through the mountains ahead of an early snowfall, Zephyrine must choose between selling the compass to clear her debts and using it to lead a stranded village to safety. She spends it — shattering it into a guiding shard for the villagers — and clears her debts instead by testifying against the Syndicate, finally measuring life in years.
about_author: Mirabel Zhou is a former river guide who writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on the northern coast. Her stories follow people who outrun their pasts and the landscapes that refuse to let them.

chapters.title: The Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Chasing a storm across the flats to earn salvage money, she returns to find the Rivergate Syndicate has seized her truck as collateral. Her handler, Vess, offers one last job: investigate a cave the receding tide exposed. The beat is desperation masked as bravado.

chapters.title: What the Tide Leaves
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Inside the cave she finds bones, old survey marks, and a brass compass whose needle ignores north. When Syndicate enforcers arrive to take it, she flees with it and a stranger — Ivo, who was already hiding there. The beat is vertigo: her careful, measured life coming apart.

chapters.title: A Needle That Lies Kindly
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the run, he explains the compass belonged to his family and points toward survival, not direction. Zephyrine doesn't believe him until it leads them around a rockslide minutes before it falls. The beat is reluctant alliance, two liars learning each other's tells.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They learn the only pass out closes with early snows — six days away — while Syndicate riders close from behind. The compass needle bends toward a mountain village that isn't on any route they'd choose. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Honest Work at Bad Altitudes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the village of Lowmark, the compass pulls them to a collapsed mine where survivors are trapped. Digging them out costs them a day and reveals the Syndicate's plan: buy the valley's water rights once the snows strand everyone. The beat is the first taste of belonging she hasn't paid for.

chapters.title: Vess Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Catching up under a flag of truce, Vess offers Zephyrine full debt forgiveness for the compass, painting the Syndicate as saviors who'll guide the valley through winter — for a price. Zephyrine nearly says yes. The beat is temptation, honest and reasonable-sounding.

chapters.title: The Long White Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The storm arrives early. Separated from Zephyrine in whiteout, Ivo must trust the compass without her and finds it leading him back toward danger — toward her. The beat is faith tested: what do you follow when the instrument and your fear disagree?

chapters.title: Snowbound Bargains
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Trapped with Vess in a waystation, Zephyrine learns the Syndicate intends to seal the pass and starve the valley into selling. She steals the compass back during the night, wounding Vess's trust but not Vess. The beat is the point of no return — justice chosen over survival arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. In the climax, Zephyrine and Ivo lead the villagers through the closing pass using the compass, with Syndicate riders behind and avalanche ahead. Zephyrine shatters the compass, giving each family a shard that holds true long enough to see them through. The beat is sacrifice as navigation.

chapters.title: Measured in Years
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Spring. Testimony from the valley brings down the Syndicate; her debt dies with it. Ivo leaves to rebuild his family's map house, and she chooses to stay in Lowmark — the first place she's stopped counting miles. The final image: a broken compass on her mantel, needle resting at last. The beat is arrival.
